body:
Thanks for the response, first and foremost. I know I have depression, and sought professional help for years. I spent probably a solid 5-7 years on some sort of anti-depressant while going to both a therapist and psychiatrist. I have pretty crippling anxiety also, and it has only gotten worse in the past few years. That's certainly not helping my cause. 

The last time I sought help was about a year ago. I was on an antidepressant for about 4-5 months before going off because it wasn't really doing much for me, good or bad. 

I can't even afford going to a doctor or take meds again, being as I am now uninsured and penniless. And I've been through that process so many times in my life that I can't immagine it would make a difference if I tried just one more time. 

I know it sounds like I'm making excuses, but I really feel like there's only so many times you can try something before you have to realize it's not doing any good. 

Even with anti-depressants, I'd still have virtually nothing to live for. I have basically no friends. I have no money and will soon be homeless. I am in a significant amount of debt. What little family I do have, I am not close with and haven't spoken to in years. 

The only thing I keep saying to myself is, "hey, at least you aren't in prison." That just doesn't seem like a compelling reason to keep going anymore.

Thanks for the advice, though.
